This happens across multiple playlists and on three different computers. > > I have updated AdGuard's filters, refreshed YouTube, and tested with another ad-blocking extension disabled. The problem persists. > > **Important test results:** > - With AdGuard enabled, the repeat function switches off between songs. > - With AdGuard disabled, repeat stays enabled across several songs, but YouTube advertisements appear. > - Screenshots showing both situations are attached. > > I have used AdGuard successfully for a long time, and YouTube's repeat function previously worked correctly. > > Please investigate whether an AdGuard filtering rule is interfering with YouTube's playlist repeat function. <!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"eb941fe79eca57dd95366ae86963c2a1cdf1c55325b4f7e190b3aa2e662c0e20"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report is filed for aternos.com, but that host serves only a 220-byte empty frameset (its only child frame is about:⁠blank) on every path — index, 302-catch-all and ad-slot scans show no content — while the reporter's screenshots show aternos.org, which this session may not open. With no reachable page and no captured detector request, no rule can be written or validated; the report needs maintainer review rather than a fabricated selector.

## Missing information

- Reported host aternos.com serves an empty placeholder frameset; the real site (aternos.org) is off-origin and cannot be loaded: The issue's trusted URL is http:⁠//aternos.com/. In the locked adguard_cli session the reported origin returns a 220-byte frameset placeholder with an empty frame for /, and every path (/en/, /servers/) 302s to /index.html, which is the same placeholder:⁠ no visible text, no ad slots (inspect_ad_slots candidateCount 0), no third-party requests beyond local.adguard.org. The reporter's own screenshots show aternos.org, and the repository already keeps an anti-adblock rule family for aternos.org in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt, but open_page refuses any navigation to a different origin ("URL must remain on configured issue origin 'http:⁠//aternos.com'"), including https:⁠//aternos.com/. Nothing in the run instruction or guidance says how to validate a report whose reported host no longer serves the site whose symptom the reporter documented. Live evidence for the reported ads and anti-adblock wall therefore cannot be collected in any session this environment allows.

## Artifacts
